pred_ddx.label: Urinary tract infection with Escherichia coli

Urothelial carcinoma: The patient's significant smoking history, symptoms of UTI, and CT scan findings of irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall are consistent with urothelial carcinoma, a common type of bladder cancer associated with smoking.
Urinary tract infection with Escherichia: The patient's symptoms of fever, flank pain, and foul-smelling urine, along with the growth of Escherichia coli in blood and urine cultures, confirm the diagnosis of a urinary tract infection. The patient's immunosuppressed state due to lung transplantation and prophylactic antimicrobial therapy may have contributed to the development of this infection.
